request.title: Launch pricing: paid upfront or subscription?
request.why: Pricing is a business call, and changing it after launch affects early buyers' trust.
request.context: The app passed review and only needs a price to ship. Of 5 comparable apps, 3 are paid upfront ($1.99–$7.99) and 2 are subscriptions (from $2.99/mo). Core features work offline, so there is no ongoing server cost per user.

options.label: Paid upfront, $3.49
options.detail: One-time revenue; simplest for buyers who expect to pay for quality.

options.label: Free + $2.49/month
options.detail: Recurring revenue, lower conversion; needs restore-purchase and downgrade handling.

request.rec_reason: No ongoing cost to cover, and paid upfront is the simplest model that matches this audience.

evidence.claim: 3 of the 5 closest competitors charge upfront; their average is about $3.90.
A subscription adds about 2 days of work for restore and expiry handling.

request.undo: The price can be changed in the store console at any time; existing buyers are unaffected.

response.conditions: If first-week conversion is under 2%, come back and ask about a subscription.
response.standing_rule: New apps launch paid upfront by default; don't start with a subscription.

ack.note: Price set to $3.49 and the build is submitted; first-week conversion will be in the weekly report.
